title: Report Chain
prompt:
You receive a valid organization tree as `relations`, where every row is `[manager, report_1, report_2, ...]`. There is exactly one root. Preserve the report order in each row. One indentation level is four dots (`....`).

Implement these functions:

- `build_children(relations) -> (children, root)`: return an adjacency mapping and the root name.
- `render_full_chain(relations) -> str`: render the entire tree in pre-order, one employee per line.
- `all_skip_level_pairs(relations) -> list[tuple[str, str]]`: return all `(manager, employee)` pairs whose employee is exactly two reporting levels below that manager, in pre-order traversal order.
- `render_chain_for(relations, target) -> str`: render the path from the root through `target`, then the full subtree below target. Print target only once.
- `lowest_common_manager(relations, employee1, employee2) -> str`: return the lowest shared manager.

You may assume the input is valid and every queried employee exists. Target O(n) preprocessing and traversal time for the whole hierarchy.

example.reasoning: A pre-order DFS renders reports in the order given by each relation row.
